cues.text: The Children's Book Festival is coming up again soon, and here to tell us all about it is the festival's organiser, Jenny Morgan. So, tell us what we can expect this year, Jenny.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well, as usual, we've got five days of action-packed exciting events for children, with writers coming from all over the country getting involved.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Just to give you an idea of what's on offer in the workshops, first of all, there's a very special event called Super Heroes.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: This is a chance for deaf children to share their reading experiences with author Madeline Gordon, who is herself hearing impaired.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Just Do It is a practical workshop, led by the well-known illustrator Mark Kean, who will take participants on a magical journey to faraway lands with an opportunity for aspiring actors to do some role-play.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Count On Me is an inspiring and entertaining look at the issues of friendship for 13 to 14-year-olds.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: It looks at some of the friendships described in popular books and asks participants to compare these with their own experiences.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Speak Up is part of a series of workshops on the subject of mental health.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: This is a creative writing workshop encouraging children to describe situations where young people experience loneliness.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: A recent survey revealed that children can be lonely even when they're at home with their families.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Jump for Joy, as many of you will know, is the heartwarming, best-selling story by Nina Caron about a young girl's trip to visit her relatives in India.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: It recently received the gold medal at the Waterford Awards.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Nina will get children to celebrate the word joy by writing a poem.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Sticks and Stones is the beautifully illustrated picture book for young readers about a community who organise an African Caribbean festival to help local children learn about their Jamaican roots.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: This will be a musical event where children will have the chance to play steel drums.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: This is bound to be very popular, so please book as soon as possible.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Thanks Jenny, that all sounds really interesting.
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: I'm just wondering if you have a favourite book you could recommend for our readers?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: It's hard to choose, but alive and kicking is definitely worth mentioning.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: You won't have heard of the writer as it's her first book, which is really impressive.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: It's basically the teenage diary of a boy from Somalia who comes to live in the UK.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: It deals with the serious issue of immigration and all the challenges the boy has to face at school and with the language barrier etc.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Usually books like this are quite sad, but this one actually made me cry with laughter. On each page there are simple but hilarious black and white stick drawings of the boy with his friends and teachers.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: At the end of each diary entry there are new English words the boy learns each day which may help develop some children's vocabulary.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: I think my kids would enjoy that. What about any advice for parents on how to encourage their children to read more?
cues.speaker: MAN

cues.text: Well, this is something I get asked about a lot. There are so many distractions for kids these days that it can be hard to find time for reading.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: One thing I'd say is to make time to sit down with your child and share books with them.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: A lot of parents give up reading aloud to their children as soon as they learn to read independently, but this is a mistake.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: It's good to read more advanced books to them as it helps to develop their vocabulary.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: If you don't have time for this, then let them listen to audiobooks.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Often they'll want to read books they've listened to for themselves.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: I think it's a good idea to make a mental note of the type of books your child is reading.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Often they just read the same genre all the time, which can get a bit boring.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: You can introduce new authors and genres to them.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Librarian should be able to help you with this.
cues.speaker: Jenny

cues.text: Well, Jenny, I think that's really useful.
cues.speaker: MAN
